title: Finite presentation of a flat module after the boundary blowup
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, $f:X\to S$ a morphism locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], $\mathcal M$ a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module flat over $S$, and $U\subset S$ a quasi-compact open such that $\mathcal M|_{X_U}$ is finitely presented. There is a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal J\subset\mathcal O_S$ with $V(\mathcal J)=S\setminus U$. For any such $\mathcal J$, its blowup $c:T=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}S\to S$ [def-nagata-global-blowup] is $U$-admissible, $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $U_T=c^{-1}(U)$ is quasi-compact, retrocompact (its intersection with every quasi-compact open is quasi-compact), and scheme-theoretically dense (for $j:U_T\hookrightarrow T$ the map $\mathcal O_T\to j_*\mathcal O_{U_T}$ is injective). If $p:X\times_ST\to X$ is the projection, then the module strict transform $\mathcal M^c$ is canonically $p^*\mathcal M$ and is flat over $T$ and of finite presentation as an $\mathcal O_{X\times_ST}$-module. The finite-presentation assertion is global on the entire fibre product. Module pullback is as in [def-pc-module-pullback]. Schemes and quasi-compactness conventions are as in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], quasi-coherence and finite type as in [pqf-def-coherent], finite presentation of module sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], and relative flatness as in [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Admissible blowups retain their finite-type centre ideals [def-nagata-admissible-blowup], and all module strict transforms use those specified ideals [def-trf-module-strict-transform].

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal-exists] to the qcqs scheme $S$ and the quasi-compact open $U$ to obtain a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal with zero set $S\setminus U$. Now fix any such ideal $\mathcal J$. Apply [det-nagata-boundary-divisor-cartier] to $(S,U,\mathcal J)$. It gives that $c:T=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}S\to S$ is $U$-admissible and that $U_T=c^{-1}(U)$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $T$. In particular the restriction map $\mathcal O_T\to j_*\mathcal O_{U_T}$ is injective. In Lean, convert ideal-data finite type to module-sheaf finite type using [lem-pqf-finite-type-ideal-module]. Conversely, for a specified centre whose ideal module is finite type, its kernel construction is quasi-coherent by closed-immersion pushforward [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel]. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], its affine sections are finite modules; their linear images under the ideal inclusion are exactly the affine ideals, so those ideals are finitely generated. This supplies the ideal-data finite-type hypothesis of the boundary theorem.

source.place: Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups, third paragraph; properties.tex Tag 01PH, lemma-quasi-coherent-finite-type-ideals; divisors.tex Tags 02OS and 07ZU.

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus] to $c$ and $\mathcal M$. Its hypotheses hold because $S$ is qcqs, $U$ is quasi-compact, and $\mathcal M$ is quasi-coherent, finite type and flat over $S$. Thus $T$ is qcqs and $\mathcal M^c\cong p^*\mathcal M$ canonically; this module is quasi-coherent, finite type and flat over $T$. The same clause identifies its restriction over $U$ with $\mathcal M|_{X_U}$.

source.place: Tag 080F, lemma-strict-transform-flat (2); Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform (1), and permanence of relative flatness under base change.

proof.text: By [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open], the restriction of the blowup map to U is an isomorphism. Its source is quasi-compact because U is quasi-compact and isomorphisms are quasi-compact. Transfer compactness of the open subscheme to its underlying open. The elementary Mathlib lemma IsCompact.isRetrocompact, using quasi-separatedness of the new base from Step 2, gives retrocompactness directly. The quasi-compactness of its inclusion follows from the same compactness and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence].

source.place: Tag 01PH, lemma-quasi-coherent-finite-type-ideals, and lemma-quasi-separated-quasi-compact-open-retrocompact; schemes.tex Tag 03GI, lemma-quasi-compact-permanence.

proof.text: Put $Y=X\times_ST$ and let $q:Y\to T$ be the projection. By clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], $q$ is locally of finite presentation, being a base change of $f$. Over $U_T\cong U$, Step 2 identifies $\mathcal M^c$ with the given finitely presented module $\mathcal M|_{X_U}$. Now apply [lem-trf-flat-finite-type-dense-presentation] to $(q,\mathcal M^c,U_T)$: Step 2 supplies finite type, quasi-coherence and relative flatness; Steps 1 and 3 supply schematic density and retrocompactness. It follows that $\mathcal M^c$, and hence its canonical isomorphic pullback $p^*\mathcal M$, is finitely presented on all of $Y$. The criterion imposes no quasi-compactness hypothesis on $Y$ or $X$. For the finite-presentation hypothesis, a private proved helper compares tensor pullback with the native scheme-module pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints, composes native pullbacks around the open restriction square, and uses preservation of finite presentation by native pullback. The pullback condition identifies the two source opens. Restrict the canonical quotient isomorphism from Step 2 and transfer finite presentation across it. For schematic density, apply Scheme.Hom.app_injective to the quasi-compact open inclusion and rewrite its target open as the intersection with the preserved open. These are interface identifications, not new unproved statements.

lean.statement: theorem flatModulePresentationAfterBoundaryBlowup {X S : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (F : X.Modules) [hF : F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] (hflat : F.IsFlatOver f) (U : S.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set S)) (hUfp : ((restrictFunctor (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι).obj F).IsFinitePresentation) : (∃ I : S.IdealSheafData, I.toModules.IsFiniteType ∧ (I.support : Set S) = (U : Set S)ᶜ) ∧ ∀ (I : S.IdealSheafData) (hI : I.toModules.IsFiniteType), (I.support : Set S) = (U : Set S)ᶜ → (∃ B : IsAdmissible S U, B.I = I) ∧ CompactSpace I.blowup ∧ QuasiSeparatedSpace I.blowup ∧ IsCompact ((I.blowupMap ⁻¹ᵁ U : I.blowup.Opens) : Set I.blowup) ∧ IsRetrocompact ((I.blowupMap ⁻¹ᵁ U : I.blowup.Opens) : Set I.blowup) ∧ IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant (I.blowupMap ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι ∧ IsIso (cokernel.π (kernel.ι (moduleStrictTransformRestriction f I F))) ∧ (@moduleStrictTransform _ _ f I hI F hF).IsFlatOver (pullback.snd f I.blowupMap) ∧ (@moduleStrictTransform _ _ f I hI F hF).IsFinitePresentation
